title: When the Parish Turns Anew
premise: Dominic Yarrow is hired to investigate the disappearance of schoolteacher Maren Oduya, whose diary keeps receiving entries dated after she vanished. As Dominic's photographic memory cross-references the diary against the case file, she realizes the killer has access to the investigation itself and is staging evidence to frame an innocent man before trial. The trail leads to the parish where Maren once taught, and to a beloved figure hiding behind decades of quiet service. Dominic closes the case by baiting the killer with a falsified file entry, forcing a confession recorded at the old church, and choosing at last to stop being invisible herself.
about_author: Ada Almeida is a former parish archivist who spent years cataloguing the small secrets of coastal communities. She writes mysteries about people whose careful lives conceal extraordinary memories and quiet courage.

chapters.title: The Diary That Kept Writing
chapters.summary: Dominic Yarrow, POV. Hired by Maren Oduya's sister, Dominic reads the missing woman's diary and freezes: entries continue eleven days past her disappearance, in handwriting that matches perfectly. Her photographic memory flags a single altered word. Emotional beat: professional detachment cracking into unease as the impossible detail refuses to be dismissed.

chapters.title: A Man Already Convicted
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Police have charged groundskeeper Tomas Reyes; the trial begins in six weeks. Reviewing the file from memory, Dominic notices evidence was logged in an order only someone inside the investigation could arrange. Emotional beat: dawning suspicion that the case is a performance staged for investigators like her.

chapters.title: What the Parish Remembers
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV, visiting St. Brigid's parish where Maren taught. Congregants offer warm, contradictory recollections; Father Ambrose Hale is gracious but steers every conversation away from Maren's final months. Emotional beat: belonging offered freely, which unsettles a woman who has always kept herself invisible.

chapters.title: Ink and Water
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Forensic analysis shows the post-disappearance entries were written on paper exposed to the same damp as the original diary pages—someone had access for weeks. A caretaker mentions seeing lights in the vestry late at night. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: The File That Fights Back
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. A key exhibit goes missing from police storage hours after she requests it; her own name appears in a leaked copy of the internal log. Someone is watching her work. Emotional beat: isolation and paranoia—the investigator realizing she has become part of the record.

chapters.title: Maren's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: reconstructed chapters of Maren's true diary, hidden in a student's keepsake box, surface via a former pupil. They reveal she discovered financial irregularities in the parish restoration fund. Emotional beat: grief and tenderness—the victim becomes a person, not a puzzle.

chapters.title: Confession, Overheard
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Concealed in the confessional, she hears Father Hale take a call, quoting case-file numbers verbatim—including details never made public. His voice is calm, rehearsed, protective of something. Emotional beat: horror braided with reluctant compassion for a man who believes he is saving his parish.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Confronted privately, Hale admits he moved Maren's body and forged the diary to protect the parish—and its donors—from scandal, insisting it was mercy. He offers Dominic a place, a purpose, silence. Emotional beat: temptation; for one night, invisibility feels like safety.

chapters.title: The Baited Page
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. She plants a false entry in the trial file claiming the original diary survived in a bank vault. Hale breaks into the vault the night before proceedings open; Dominic and police wait inside. Emotional beat: cold clarity—her memory, once a burden, becomes the trap itself.

chapters.title: When the Parish Turns Anew
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Hale confesses on record; Tomas Reyes walks free. At Maren's memorial, Dominic reads her recovered words aloud, letting the congregation see her hands shake. Emotional beat: resolution and transformation—she closes the case, then opens herself, no longer willing to stay invisible.
